papers.why: Targeting Ube3a-ATS with a poly(A) cassette unsilences paternal Ube3a and improves motor, cognitive, and electrophysiological defects in an Angelman syndrome mouse model.

papers.title: Altered ultrasonic vocalization and impaired learning and memory in Angelman syndrome mouse model with a large maternal deletion from Ube3a to Gabrb3.
papers.summary: The paper generated and characterized mice carrying a 1.6-Mb maternal deletion from Ube3a to Gabrb3 that also deletes Atp10a, creating a model molecularly similar to the contiguous 15q11–q13 deletion form of Angelman syndrome. Maternal deletion mice showed seizures, abnormal EEG activity, motor, learning and memory, anxiety-related, and ultrasonic-vocalization abnormalities, whereas paternal deletion mice were generally phenotypically normal; homozygous deletion mice showed perinatal lethality and cleft palate.
papers.why: The engineered maternal-deletion mouse models the contiguous 15q11-q13 deletion form of Angelman syndrome and exhibits seizures, EEG abnormalities, communication changes, and cognitive and motor impairments.

papers.title: Delta rhythmicity is a reliable EEG biomarker in Angelman syndrome: a parallel mouse and human analysis.
papers.summary: The paper identifies increased delta rhythmicity, quantified as delta power and within-session delta dynamics, as a robust EEG biomarker of Angelman syndrome in children and in the Ube3a m−/p+ mouse model. Delta abnormalities were generalized across the neocortex during wakefulness and sleep, were strongest at younger ages, and could serve as acute and longitudinal outcome measures for Angelman syndrome trials.
papers.why: Parallel mouse and human data establish EEG delta rhythmicity as a reproducible clinical and preclinical biomarker for Angelman syndrome.

papers.title: A behavioral test battery for mouse models of Angelman syndrome: a powerful tool for testing drugs and novel Ube3a mutants.
papers.summary: This study establishes a standardized, repeatable behavioral test battery across several independently derived Ube3a mouse lines, while showing that most phenotypes are strongly dependent on genetic background and the audiogenic seizure assay is particularly robust and pharmacologically reversible. Minocycline and levodopa did not improve the measured behavioral phenotypes, agreeing with their lack of efficacy in prior Angelman syndrome clinical trials.
papers.why: The paper validates a standardized preclinical testing battery across multiple Angelman mouse models and tests the responsiveness to minocycline and levodopa.

papers.title: Antisense oligonucleotide treatment rescues UBE3A expression and multiple phenotypes of an Angelman syndrome mouse model.
papers.summary: A phosphorothioate and locked nucleic acid gapmer antisense oligonucleotide, RTR26266, degraded mouse Ube3a-ATS and reinstated neuronal UBE3A after intracerebroventricular delivery at P1 or P21 in Ube3am−/p+ Angelman syndrome mice. Treatment fully rescued audiogenic seizure susceptibility and improved several neurobehavioral phenotypes, but did not rescue marble burying or nest building, and produced only partial or nonsignificant rescue of motor coordination, microcephaly, body weight, and hippocampal long-term potentiation.
papers.why: The study directly demonstrates that an ASO targeting Ube3a-ATS restores UBE3A and rescues multiple behavioral, motor, and seizure phenotypes in an Angelman mouse model.

papers.title: Linoleic acid improves PIEZO2 dysfunction in a mouse model of Angelman Syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper finds that loss of UBE3A reduces F-actin and PIEZO2 expression/function in Angelman syndrome models, producing impaired mechanical excitability in sensory neurons. Linoleic acid increases PIEZO2 activity in cells and neurons from individuals with Angelman syndrome, while a safflower-oil-enriched diet improves gait parameters in Ube3a-deficient mice without improving rotarod performance or demonstrated enhancement of nociception.
papers.why: The study shows that linoleic acid restores PIEZO2 activity in patient-derived neurons and improves gait-related deficits in an Angelman mouse model.

papers.title: Angelman syndrome genotypes manifest varying degrees of clinical severity and developmental impairment.
papers.summary: In a natural-history cohort of 250 individuals with Angelman syndrome, genotype was associated with global developmental and clinical severity: deletion and paternal uniparental disomy genotypes were generally more impaired than non-deletion or missense-variant genotypes, while class 1 versus class 2 deletion differences were small. The Bayley Scales of Infant Development, Third Edition, Preschool Language Scale, Fourth Edition, Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales, Second Edition, and the Angelman syndrome Clinical Severity Scale quantified functional domains, but each had genotype- or population-specific limitations.
papers.why: This large natural-history study provides standardized clinical outcome measures and quantitative severity data for Angelman syndrome across genetic subtypes.

papers.title: Abnormal coherence and sleep composition in children with Angelman syndrome: a retrospective EEG study.
papers.summary: This exploratory retrospective EEG study identifies quantitative Angelman syndrome phenotypes: increased long-range EEG coherence during wakefulness, increased long-range gamma-band coherence during NREM sleep, and reduced sleep-spindle number and duration. The findings support coherence and spindle measures as candidate biomarkers or clinical-trial outcome measures, but their robustness, sleep-state dependence, and relationship to behavioral outcomes require confirmation in controlled studies.
papers.why: The study validates disease-specific EEG readouts in children with Angelman syndrome and proposes them as biomarkers and trial target-engagement measures.

papers.title: Secreted retrovirus-like GAG-domain-containing protein PEG10 is regulated by UBE3A and is involved in Angelman syndrome pathophysiology.
papers.summary: The paper identifies PEG10-RF1/2 as a UBE3A-regulated, proteasome-dependent protein that is elevated in Angelman syndrome patient-derived neurons and present in extracellular vesicles. UBE3A reinstatement or PEG10 reduction produces overlapping rescue of the AS neuronal transcriptome, while forced PEG10-RF1/2 overexpression impairs neuronal migration during mouse cortical development; patient-brain evidence for persistent PEG10 upregulation remains limited.
papers.why: Antisense-mediated UBE3A reinstatement and PEG10 reduction rescued disease-associated neuronal changes, directly providing tested therapeutic and model-system approaches.

papers.title: Angelman syndrome-derived neurons display late onset of paternal UBE3A silencing.
papers.summary: The study established AS_∆3 induced pluripotent stem cells from an Angelman syndrome patient carrying a three-base-pair deletion in maternal UBE3A, preserving the PWS-SRO imprint and allowing both parental UBE3A alleles to be distinguished. During differentiation into mature neurons, paternal SNHG14 expression increased strongly and was associated with late paternal UBE3A silencing beginning around day 28, while total UBE3A expression increased and protein levels remained comparable to undifferentiated cells.
papers.why: The study created and characterized a stable patient-derived iPSC model that reproduces delayed paternal UBE3A silencing during neuronal differentiation.

papers.title: A multidisciplinary approach and consensus statement to establish standards of care for Angelman syndrome.
papers.summary: This consensus review describes Angelman syndrome as a neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss of maternally expressed UBE3A in the central nervous system and proposes standards for diagnosis and lifelong care. It identifies supportive interventions for seizures, sleep, behavior, feeding, mobility, and systemic complications while reporting negative clinical trials for several candidate disease-modifying or symptomatic therapies.
papers.why: This consensus framework provides disease-specific clinical management practices and outcome domains across seizures, development, sleep, movement, feeding, communication, and other Angelman manifestations.

papers.title: Translational outcomes in a full gene deletion of ubiquitin protein ligase E3A rat model of Angelman syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper establishes a Sprague-Dawley rat model with deletion of the entire Ube3a gene that reproduces parent-of-origin-dependent behavioral and neuroanatomical abnormalities of Angelman syndrome. The model provides communication, motor, learning, and MRI outcomes intended for preclinical testing of gene and molecular therapies, while several normal and null findings help delimit the phenotype.
papers.why: The study creates and validates a comprehensive Angelman rat model with behavioral, neuroanatomical, and preclinical outcome measures for testing gene and molecular therapies.

papers.title: Functional rescue in an Angelman syndrome model following treatment with lentivector transduced hematopoietic stem cells.
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates that transplantation of human CD34+ hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells transduced with a UBE3A-expressing lentiviral vector prevented or reversed motor, cognitive, gait, and EEG abnormalities in neonatal and adult Ube3a-deficient Angelman syndrome mice. In vitro and engraftment experiments showed functional UBE3A expression, preserved multilineage differentiation, and increased UBE3A-positive cells in the treated mouse cortex, although neuronal colocalization was not demonstrated.
papers.why: The study demonstrates functional rescue of motor, cognitive, and EEG phenotypes in an Angelman syndrome mouse model using transplanted, UBE3A-expressing hematopoietic cells.

papers.title: Delayed loss of UBE3A reduces the expression of Angelman syndrome-associated phenotypes.
papers.summary: Conditional deletion studies in mice show that loss of UBE3A during embryonic development produces Angelman syndrome-like behavioral deficits and audiogenic seizure susceptibility, whereas deletion at 3 or 12 weeks causes substantially fewer phenotypes. The findings indicate that UBE3A reactivation therapies may need to begin early in life, while sustained expression into adulthood may be required for optimal benefit and for normal forced-swim behavior.
papers.why: The conditional mouse study provides direct evidence about when UBE3A loss produces Angelman phenotypes and informs the timing and duration of gene-reactivation therapies.

papers.title: Reelin supplementation recovers synaptic plasticity and cognitive deficits in a mouse model for Angelman syndrome.
papers.summary: In a UBE3A-null mouse model of Angelman syndrome, a single bilateral intraventricular injection of recombinant Reelin improved hippocampal long-term potentiation, restored dendritic spine density, and rescued contextual fear conditioning and delayed spatial memory deficits. Reelin treatment did not improve locomotion, anxiety, motor coordination, or cued fear conditioning, and the study also found altered Reelin protein profiles in AS mouse brain and post-mortem human AS cortex.
papers.why: Direct intraventricular Reelin treatment in an Angelman syndrome mouse model restored synaptic plasticity, dendritic spine density, and hippocampus-dependent learning and memory.

papers.title: Delta power robustly predicts cognitive function in Angelman syndrome.
papers.summary: In 82 individuals with Angelman syndrome, EEG delta power strongly and inversely predicted cognitive function, with the mixed-effects model explaining 93.74% of Bayley Cognitive Score variance and 94.55% in cross-validation. The relationship was robust across sleep and wake states, EEG montages, and artifact conditions, and delta power also predicted receptive communication, expressive communication, and fine motor scores but not gross motor scores.
papers.why: In a large Angelman syndrome cohort, EEG delta power accurately predicted cognitive scores and was validated as a robust objective endpoint for treatment-response trials.

papers.title: Angelman syndrome-associated ubiquitin ligase UBE3A/E6AP mutants interfere with the proteolytic activity of the proteasome.
papers.summary: The paper shows that catalytically inactive Angelman syndrome-associated UBE3A mutants bind the proteasome S5a/Rpn10 subunit more strongly than wild-type UBE3A, increase S5a ubiquitination, and inhibit overall proteasomal proteolytic activity. Ectopic S5a reverses the inhibition of Mdm2-dependent p53 degradation, supporting an S5a-dependent mechanism through which loss or dysfunction of UBE3A could impair proteostasis in Angelman syndrome.
papers.why: Experimental data show that catalytically inactive Angelman-associated UBE3A mutants bind the proteasome and inhibit its activity, identifying a potentially actionable disease mechanism.

papers.title: Maternal disruption of Ube3a leads to increased expression of Ube3a-ATS in trans.
papers.summary: In an Angelman syndrome mouse model carrying a targeted disruption of mouse Ube3a, maternal—but not paternal—inheritance of the mutation increased paternal Ube3a-ATS expression by approximately two- to threefold. The increased antisense transcript did not significantly alter the maternal:paternal Ube3a mRNA ratio, arguing against a simple cis-silencing model in which Ube3a-ATS reduces paternal Ube3a expression.
papers.why: The study directly tested parental UBE3A-ATS regulation in an Angelman syndrome mouse model and provides mechanistic evidence about antisense-mediated imprinting.

papers.title: Normal social seeking behavior, hypoactivity and reduced exploratory range in a mouse model of Angelman syndrome.
papers.summary: In adult male Ube3a-deficient mice, the study found reduced exploratory activity but normal interest in a stranger mouse relative to wild-type littermates. Thus, these Ube3a-only deficiency models reproduce hypoactivity but not the hyperactivity or increased social-seeking behavior characteristic of human Angelman syndrome.
papers.why: The paper directly characterizes two engineered Ube3a mouse models and standardizes behavioral assays for activity, locomotion, exploration, and social approach in Angelman syndrome research.

papers.title: Prader-Willi syndrome: a review of clinical, genetic, and endocrine findings.
papers.summary: This review states that loss of maternally expressed UBE3A expression in chromosome 15q11-q13 causes Angelman syndrome, while DNA methylation analysis can distinguish Angelman syndrome from Prader-Willi syndrome. It also identifies hypopigmentation as a phenotype associated with the shared chromosome 15q11-q13 deletion but does not evaluate treatments for Angelman syndrome.
papers.why: Describes methylation analysis that detects all Prader-Willi molecular subtypes and differentiates Prader-Willi syndrome from Angelman syndrome.

papers.title: Characterization and structure-activity relationships of indenoisoquinoline-derived topoisomerase I inhibitors in unsilencing the dormant <i>Ube3a</i> gene associated with Angelman syndrome.
papers.summary: In cultured primary cortical neurons from an Angelman syndrome mouse model, all 13 tested indenoisoquinoline-derived topoisomerase I inhibitors increased expression of paternal Ube3a. Indotecan (LMP400) showed the strongest overall pharmacological profile, outperforming topotecan in efficacy and potency while retaining similar neuronal cytotoxicity, but its safety and CNS bioavailability for Angelman syndrome require in vivo assessment.
papers.why: The study directly identifies multiple topoisomerase I inhibitors that reactivate paternal UBE3A in Angelman models, with indotecan showing the strongest pharmacological profile.

papers.title: Electrophysiological Abnormalities in Angelman Syndrome Correlate With Symptom Severity.
papers.summary: In children with Angelman syndrome caused by common class I or II 15q11-q13 deletions, greater EEG delta-band power was associated cross-sectionally and longitudinally with worse cognition, communication, motor function, adaptive behavior, and earlier epilepsy onset. The study supports awake EEG, particularly delta-band power and possibly combined spatiospectral metrics, as an investigational biomarker for symptom severity and treatment trials, but the results remain correlational and require validation.
papers.why: This study directly identifies EEG abnormalities and spatial/spectral EEG features as biomarkers associated with symptom severity and longitudinal outcomes in Angelman syndrome.

papers.title: Prenatal delivery of a therapeutic antisense oligonucleotide achieves broad biodistribution in the brain and ameliorates Angelman syndrome phenotype in mice.
papers.summary: Prenatal delivery of a Ube3a-AS-targeting antisense oligonucleotide reactivated paternal UBE3A in mouse brain and partially rescued accelerating-rotarod and cue-based fear-conditioning phenotypes. Intracerebroventricular and intra-amniotic delivery both achieved broad central nervous system distribution, but dose-dependent survival effects and increased maternal aspartate aminotransferase after intracerebroventricular dosing require further safety and translational evaluation.
papers.why: This study demonstrates prenatal ASO-mediated reactivation of paternal UBE3A and phenotypic rescue in Angelman syndrome mice, with broad brain biodistribution.

papers.title: Loss of nuclear UBE3A activity is the predominant cause of Angelman syndrome in individuals carrying UBE3A missense mutations.
papers.summary: Functional testing of 31 Angelman syndrome-associated UBE3A missense mutants showed that loss of nuclear localization and loss of E3 ubiquitin ligase activity were the predominant mechanisms of dysfunction, accounting for 55% and 29% of variants, respectively. The localization and bacterial ubiquitination assays provide a two-step framework for assessing the pathogenicity of novel UBE3A missense variants, although variants without detectable deficits in these assays may still be clinically pathogenic.
papers.why: The study provides disease-specific functional assays and data for assessing UBE3A missense variants relevant to Angelman syndrome diagnosis and treatment development.

papers.title: Neurodevelopmental profile in Angelman syndrome: more than low intelligence quotient.
papers.summary: This observational study characterizes a broad neurodevelopmental phenotype in 10 children with molecularly confirmed Angelman syndrome, including severe motor, cognitive, communication, adaptive, behavioural, and neurovisual impairment. It also identifies standardized assessment instruments as feasible tools for early domain-specific assessment and planning of tailored rehabilitation, while noting genotype- and measure-dependent differences and substantial floor or ceiling effects.
papers.why: The study validates a detailed standardized assessment battery for motor, cognitive, adaptive, communicative, behavioral, and neurovisual outcomes in molecularly confirmed Angelman syndrome.

papers.title: A Conceptual Model of Angelman Syndrome and Review of Relevant Clinical Outcomes Assessments (COAs).
papers.summary: Interviews with caregivers and clinicians generated a conceptual model of Angelman syndrome spanning cognitive, behavioral, sensory-compulsive, physical, and patient/caregiver impact domains and assessed six clinical outcome assessment instruments. All six instruments captured some relevant Angelman syndrome concepts, but each had irrelevant items, interpretive problems, or important omissions, and no single instrument covered all relevant domains.
papers.why: This study develops and evaluates an Angelman syndrome conceptual model and assesses existing clinical outcome instruments for capturing treatment-relevant symptoms and functional impacts.

papers.title: Assessing the requirements of prenatal UBE3A expression for rescue of behavioral phenotypes in a mouse model for Angelman syndrome.
papers.summary: In conditional Angelman syndrome mouse models, prenatal reactivation of maternal Ube3a around embryonic day 12.5 restored normal performance on most assessed behavioral tasks. Paternal Ube3a was biallelically expressed prenatally and became fully silenced during the first postnatal week, but loss of that paternal contribution did not significantly worsen the measured phenotypes, suggesting that approximately 50% prenatal UBE3A protein is sufficient for the tested outcomes.
papers.why: This study directly identifies the developmental timing and expression threshold for UBE3A rescue in an Angelman syndrome mouse model and demonstrates behavioral rescue after late prenatal reactivation.

papers.title: Early Developmental EEG and Seizure Phenotypes in a Full Gene Deletion of Ubiquitin Protein Ligase E3A Rat Model of Angelman Syndrome.
papers.summary: A complete maternal Ube3a-deletion rat model reproduced age-dependent cortical and hippocampal delta-power increases, spontaneous epileptiform activity, prolonged post-PTZ recovery, and reduced hyperthermia seizure threshold, while showing no difference in PTZ seizure threshold or generalized audiogenic seizures. The study supports quantitative EEG delta power as a candidate Angelman syndrome biomarker and the rat model for preclinical EEG, seizure, and therapeutic studies.
papers.why: Establishes a preclinical Angelman syndrome rat model with quantitative EEG and seizure phenotypes usable for biomarker and therapeutic studies.

papers.title: Chromosome 15 Imprinting Disorders: Genetic Laboratory Methodology and Approaches.
papers.summary: This review describes the molecular causes, phenotypes, and step-wise genetic testing strategies for Angelman syndrome and related chromosome 15 imprinting disorders. It emphasizes methylation testing for initial diagnosis, followed by SNP microarray, MS–MLPA, FISH, genotyping, or sequencing approaches to resolve Angelman syndrome molecular subclasses and inform prognosis, counseling, surveillance, and care.
papers.why: The review directly presents genetic diagnostic methods and testing approaches for Angelman syndrome and related chromosome 15 imprinting disorders.

papers.title: Electroencephalographic (EEG) Biomarkers in Genetic Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
papers.summary: This review finds that qualitative and quantitative EEG findings, especially increased rhythmic delta power, can identify and characterize Angelman syndrome and correlate with epilepsy, developmental performance, cognition, and symptom severity. It also summarizes evidence that EEG changes can track response to minocycline, exogenous ketones, and preclinical lentivector-based stem cell gene therapy, while emphasizing that increased delta power is not Angelman syndrome-specific.
papers.why: The paper directly evaluates quantitative EEG biomarkers in Angelman syndrome and reports correlation of delta power with developmental disability and seizure burden.

papers.title: Ube3a unsilencer for the potential treatment of Angelman syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper identifies (S)-PHA533533 as a stereoselective small molecule that downregulates UBE3A-ATS/Ube3a-ATS and restores paternal UBE3A/Ube3a expression in Angelman syndrome model neurons, including patient-derived human iPSC neurons. A single peripheral injection produced widespread, though incomplete and not yet therapeutically validated, UBE3A reinstatement across the brain of juvenile Angelman syndrome model mice.
papers.why: Shows that (S)-PHA533533 downregulates Ube3a-ATS and reactivates paternal UBE3A in Angelman model mice and patient-derived neurons.

papers.title: Loss of hierarchical imprinting regulation at the Prader-Willi/Angelman syndrome locus in human iPSCs.
papers.summary: The paper shows that Angelman syndrome patient-derived iPSCs retain the expected paternal-only PWS imprinting center pattern but develop recurrent, reprogramming-associated methylation abnormalities. Most notably, MKRN3 DMR becomes hypermethylated independently of PWS-IC status, demonstrating loss of hierarchical imprinting control and requiring screening of iPSCs used for disease modeling.
papers.why: The study generates patient-derived iPSC models for Angelman syndrome and characterizes their imprinting defects, providing a concrete model system and assay for disease research.

papers.title: Antisense oligonucleotide therapy rescues disturbed brain rhythms and sleep in juvenile and adult mouse models of Angelman syndrome.
papers.summary: In juvenile or adult maternal Ube3aΔe6 knockout mice, a single intracerebroventricular injection of Ube3a-ATS-targeting antisense oligonucleotides reactivated paternal Ube3a, increased Ube3a protein, and improved abnormal EEG rhythms and rapid eye movement sleep. The treatment did not significantly reverse cortical poly-spikes, and responses varied with treatment age, ASO identity, elapsed time, and degree of Ube3a restoration.
papers.why: Ube3a-ATS antisense oligonucleotides in Angelman syndrome mouse models rescue EEG rhythm abnormalities and sleep disturbance and establish measurable efficacy endpoints.

papers.title: Visual Sequences Drive Experience-Dependent Plasticity in Mouse Anterior Cingulate Cortex.
papers.summary: Repeated visual-sequence training induces a latency-based form of experience-dependent plasticity in mouse anterior cingulate cortex, whereas the Ube3am−/p+ Angelman syndrome model retains normal visual sequence encoding but lacks this ACC plasticity. V1 sequence plasticity, ACC sequence encoding, and ACC oddball responses remain normal in the model, suggesting a selective impairment in experience-dependent plasticity within ACC circuits.
papers.why: The study uses a mouse model associated with Angelman syndrome and a visual-sequence stimulation assay to quantify experience-dependent circuit plasticity.

papers.title: Autism-linked UBE3A gain-of-function mutation causes interneuron and behavioral phenotypes when inherited maternally or paternally in mice.
papers.summary: The paper establishes that the autism-linked UBE3A T485A mutation, modeled in mice as Ube3a T503A, causes gain-of-function activity, embryonic expansion of a Zcchc12-lineage interneuron population, and parent-of-origin-dependent behavioral phenotypes. Its molecular and behavioral phenotypes differ from Angelman syndrome models, but the model and functional assays provide tools for distinguishing UBE3A gain-of-function from Angelman syndrome–associated loss of function.
papers.why: Engineers and characterizes UBE3A mutant mice with parent-of-dependent neurodevelopmental phenotypes, providing a mechanistically relevant model and assays for UBE3A biology.

papers.title: Identification of disease-linked hyperactivating mutations in UBE3A through large-scale functional variant analysis.
papers.summary: The paper shows that Angelman syndrome results from loss of maternal UBE3A, whereas hyperactivating UBE3A variants—particularly Q585E/Q588E—produce distinct neurodevelopmental phenotypes rather than Angelman syndrome. A BAR assay functionally classifies UBE3A variants, and complementary biochemical, biophysical, and mouse studies show that hyperactivation is associated with altered exosite ubiquitin binding, increased substrate degradation, delayed motor development, and reduced early-life communication.
papers.why: This study develops a functional UBE3A variant assay and uses a disease-linked UBE3A mouse model to characterize neurodevelopmental phenotypes and mechanistic subtypes.

papers.title: HALOS: A Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics Study of Multiple Ascending Doses of ION582 in Participants With Angelman Syndrome
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of ascending doses of ION582 administered intrathecally in participants with Angelman syndrome.

papers.title: BEACON - Phase III Clinical Study of Rugonersen in Angelman Syndrome.
papers.summary: Purpose of the study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of intrathecally administered rugonersen in pediatric and adult participants with Angelman syndrome.

papers.title: A Trial of Levodopa in Angelman Syndrome
papers.summary:
This study is designed to determine whether levodopa will lead to an improvement in the development and tremor in children with Angelman syndrome (AS).

It has been suggested that levodopa, a medication that is usually used to treat Parkinson disease in adults, may help children with AS in their overall development and reduce the tremor that some of them have.

If levodopa is found to be beneficial for children with AS, this could lead to a new treatment for AS.

Funding Source - FDA-OOPD

papers.title: A Phase 1/2 Study of the Safety and Efficacy of MVX-220 in Angelman Syndrome
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of MVX-220 gene therapy in children and adults with Angelman syndrome with UBE3A gene deletion, uniparental disomy, or imprinting center defect genotypes.

papers.title: A Study of the Safety and Tolerability of GTX-102 in Children With Angelman Syndrome
papers.summary: The primary objective of the study is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of multiple-ascending doses of GTX-102 administered by intrathecal (IT) injection to participants with Angelman Syndrome (AS).

papers.title: Nutritional Formulation for Angelman Syndrome
papers.summary: Low carbohydrate diets such as the ketogenic (KD) and low glycemic index (LGIT) diets have been shown to be effective in treating drug resistant seizures in children with Angelman syndrome (AS). The investigators hypothesize that consuming a fat based nutritional formulation with an exogenous ketone throughout the day will produce urinary ketosis in children consuming both low and high carbohydrate diets, depending upon dietary background. The nutritional formulation will provide fuel substrates that push metabolism away from carbohydrates and towards fat utilization. This research is being do

papers.title: Clinical Trial of Levodopa/Carbidopa ( Sinemet) Therapy in Angel Man Syndrome
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and effectiveness (how well a drug works) of Carbidopa/levodopa (Sinemet) in individuals with Angelman syndrome. Sinemet is a medication that helps to raise dopamine levels (a chemical that signals nerve cells) in the brain and central nervous system. There is evidence that dopamine concentrations may be abnormal in patients with Angelman syndrome. This study is investigating whether Sinemet helps motor control, intellectual function and the achievement of developmental milestones in people with Angelman syndrome

papers.title: Angelman Syndrome (AS) Biomarker Study
papers.summary: The primary objective of this study is to measure ubiquitin-protein ligase E3A (UBE3A) protein levels in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and to evaluate its utility as a biomarker in support of the development of therapies for AS.

papers.title: An Open-Label Study of the Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetics of Oral NNZ-2591 in Angelman Syndrome
papers.summary: A study of the safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics of NNZ-2591 and measures of efficacy in children and adolescents with Angelman syndrome

papers.title: Single Dose Pharmacokinetic (PK) Study
papers.summary:
The trial is a Phase 1 Single Dose PK Study in Adolescent Subjects with Fragile X syndrome (FXS) or Angelman syndrome (AS).

* The primary objective of the study is to evaluate the pharmacokinetics (PK) of OV101 following a single 5 mg dose of OV101 in adolescents with FXS or AS.
* Secondary objectives are to determine the safety and tolerability of a single 5 mg dose of OV101 in adolescents with FXS or AS.

papers.title: Assessment of the Pharmacokinetics of Circadin® in Children With Neurodevelopmental Disorders and Sleep Disturbances
papers.summary: There is increasing evidence that chronic sleep disorders in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), Angelman Syndrome (AS) and Smith-Magenis syndrome (SMS) are associated with disturbed melatonin secretion and melatonin administration has been shown to be effective in these populations. For children who have difficulties swallowing a tablet, Neurim has developed an age-appropriate Melatonin formulation in the form of mini-tablets which have the same dissolution profile as the Circadin® tablets product, thus should produce the same melatonin concentration-time profile with the same effec

papers.title: An Exploratory Open Label Study of EPI-743 (Vincerinone TM) in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder
papers.summary: The investigators hypothesize that EPI-743 may provide clinical benefit to children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.

papers.title: REVEAL: A Phase 3 Study of Obudanersen (ION582) in Angelman Syndrome
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of obudanersen in children and adults with Angelman syndrome caused by a deletion or mutation of the UBE3A gene.

papers.title: A Study in Adults and Adolescents With Angelman Syndrome (STARS)
papers.summary: The purpose of the study is to assess the safety and tolerability of oral OV101 (gaboxadol) in adult and adolescent subjects with Angelman syndrome. In addition, several exploratory efficacy outcome measures will be investigated.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Circadin® in the Treatment of Sleep Disturbances in Children With Neurodevelopment Disabilities
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to establish the efficacy and safety of Circadin in children with neurodevelopmental disorders and to determine the dose, this randomized, placebo-controlled study is planned to evaluate the efficacy of a double-blind, 13 week treatment period with Circadin 2/5mg in improving maintenance of sleep, sleep latency and additional parameters in children with neurodevelopmental disabilities. The efficacy and safety of Circadin 2/5 mg will continue to be assessed during an open-label extension period of 13 weeks.

papers.title: Long-term Extension of GTX-102 in Angelman Syndrome
papers.summary: The primary objective of the study is to evaluate the long-term safety profile of GTX-102 in participants with Angelman Syndrome (AS)

papers.title: Phase 3 Efficacy and Safety Study of GTX-102 in Pediatric Subjects With Angelman Syndrome (AS)
papers.summary: The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the effect of GTX-102 in cognitive function in participants with deletion-type Angelman Syndrome (AS).

papers.title: A Study to Investigate the Pharmacokinetics (PK) and Safety and to Provide Proof of Mechanism of Alogabat in Children and Adolescents Aged 5-17 Years With Angelman Syndrome (AS) With Deletion Genotype.
papers.summary: This is a two-part, Phase IIa, multicenter, 12-week, open-label study. Up to 56 participants with deletion AS aged 5-17 years (inclusive) will be enrolled in the study.

papers.title: Minocycline in the Treatment of Angelman Syndrome
papers.summary: There is mounting evidence to suggest that a treatment for Angelman syndrome is not just possible, but probable. The lack of known molecular targets associated with AS has hampered the development of specific therapeutics. However, a recent surge of potential therapeutics for other disorders associated with cognitive disruption has begun to be used in human clinical trials. The molecular modes of action for many of these new therapeutic agents have correlates to counter the molecular defects observed in AS. One such agent is minocycline (MC), a drug traditionally used as an antibiotic. This co

papers.title: A Study to Investigate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics (PK) and Pharmacodynamics (PD) of RO7248824 in Participants With Angelman Syndrome (AS)
papers.summary: This is a phase I, multicenter, non-randomized, adaptive, open-label, multiple ascending, intra-participant, dose-escalation study with a long-term extension (LTE) part and an optional open-label extension (OOE) part. The objective of the study is to investigate the safety, tolerability, PK and PD of RO7248824 administered intrathecally (IT) in participants with AS. Two linked sets of dose escalation cohorts are planned based on two different age groups, namely participants with AS aged ≥ 5 to ≤ 12 years in cohorts A1 to A5 (with at least 2 participants ≤ 8 years old in each cohort) and AS par

papers.title: Study on Tolerability of Levodopa/Carbidopa in Children With Angelman Syndrome
papers.summary:
This study is designed to determine the highest dose of levodopa/carbidopa that can be tolerated without any serious side effects by children with Angelman syndrome.

It has been hypothesized that levodopa may lead to an improvement in the neurodevelopment and abnormal movements (e.g. tremors) in children with Angelman syndrome.

Data from this study will be used to design a phase II trial to determine the efficacy of levodopa in treating children with Angelman syndrome.

papers.title: Dietary Supplements for the Treatment of Angelman Syndrome
papers.summary: Angelman syndrome (AS) is a complex genetic disorder that affects the nervous system. The purpose of this study is to determine the effectiveness of certain dietary supplements in treating the symptoms of AS.

papers.title: A Study To Assess Distribution Of RO7248824 In The Central Nervous System Following Single Intrathecal Doses Of [89zr] Labeled RO7248824 In Healthy Male Participants
papers.summary: The aim of Study BP41660 is to quantify the amount and concentration of \[89Zr\]DFO-RO7248824 in the brain with positron emission tomography (PET) following a single sub-pharmacological dose of RO7248824 and \[89Zr\]DFO-RO7248824 administered via IT injection to healthy participants.

papers.title: A Safety and Efficacy Study of GTX-102 in Subjects With Deletion- or Nondeletion-type Angelman Syndrome (AS)
papers.summary: The main goal of the study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of GTX-102 in participants with Angelman syndrome.

papers.title: CHAMPION: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Obudanersen (ION582) in Children and Adults With Angelman Syndrome (AS)
papers.summary: The primary purpose of the study is to evaluate efficacy of obudanersen in participants with AS due to uniparental disomy or imprinting defects (UPD/ID) as measured through expressive communication.

papers.title: Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Minocycline in Angelman Syndrome
papers.summary: RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIAL, PLACEBO COMPARED TO EVALUATE THE EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF MINOCYCLINE IN ANGELMAN SYNDROME (A-MANECE STUDY)

papers.title: An Open-Label Study to Evaluate the Long-Term Safety, Tolerability, and Efficacy of OV101 in Individuals With Angelman Syndrome
papers.summary: This open-label study (OV101-18-002) will evaluate the long-term (52 weeks) safety of OV101 in subjects with AS and provide additional OV101 treatment to those subjects who completed Study OV101-15-001 (NCT02996305). Subjects with AS who completed the pharmacokinetic Study OV101-16-001 (NCT03109756) will also be permitted to participate, provided they meet all entry criteria.

papers.title: A Study of OV101 in Individuals With Angelman Syndrome (AS)
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to assess the efficacy and safety of oral OV101 (gaboxadol) in pediatric subjects with Angelman syndrome.

papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for Angelman syndrome
Epigenetic silencing of PEG3 gene expression in human glioma cell lines.
papers.summary: The paper identifies aberrant DNA methylation of an exonic CpG island as a cause of PEG3 silencing in glioma cell lines, including gain of imprinting in four of nine cell lines. Treatment with the DNA demethylating agent 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine reversed PEG3 silencing and restored biallelic expression, but the study did not investigate UBE3A or paternal UBE3A unsilencing.

papers.title: Cyclophilin a protects Peg3 from hypermethylation and inactive histone modification.
papers.summary: In cyclophilin A knockdown P19 cells, the normally silent paternal Peg3 allele becomes biallelically methylated and acquires inactive histone modifications, resulting in Peg3 silencing. Treatment with the DNA demethylating agent 5-aza-dC reverses the silencing, demonstrating that cyclophilin A normally protects the paternal allele from epigenetic silencing.

papers.title: A Novel Long Non-Coding RNA in the hTERT Promoter Region Regulates hTERT Expression.
papers.summary: The paper identifies hTAPAS, a human antisense lncRNA at the hTERT promoter, and shows that antisense oligonucleotides can knock it down in HEK-293 cells. hTAPAS knockdown increased hTERT expression, whereas ectopic hTAPAS overexpression reduced it, demonstrating a transferable strategy for bidirectionally transcribed promoter-associated antisense RNAs but not an intervention on the UBE3A antisense transcript.

papers.title: Site-directed A → I RNA editing as a therapeutic tool: moving beyond genetic mutations.
papers.summary: This review describes site-directed A-to-I RNA editing (SDRE) as a transient therapeutic strategy for modifying endogenous RNA without changing DNA. It reports that an engineered ADAR deaminase-domain system delivered by AAV corrected a pathogenic MECP2 mutation in Rett syndrome mouse models and alleviated disease symptoms, but the paper does not discuss Angelman syndrome or the UBE3A antisense transcript.

papers.title: Therapeutic potential of natural antisense transcripts and various mechanisms involved for clinical applications and disease prevention.
papers.summary: This review identifies the UBE3A antisense transcript as an inhibitory, therapeutically accessible RNA target in Angelman syndrome and summarizes evidence that two ASO gapmers reduce Ube3a-ATS, increase paternal Ube3a expression in mice, and modestly improve cognitive deficits. It also describes an analogous NAT-targeting approach in Dravet syndrome, where oligonucleotides against SCN1A NAT partially ameliorate disease characteristics, supporting transfer of the mechanism while emphasizing delivery, off-target, and mechanistic uncertainties.

papers.title: Experimental Model Systems Used in the Preclinical Development of Nucleic Acid Therapeutics.
papers.summary: This survey reports that nucleic acid therapeutics are evaluated using patient-derived cells, induced pluripotent stem cell-derived models, organoids, organ-on-chip systems, genetically modified animals, and humanized rodents. It does not mention Angelman syndrome or provide experimental evidence concerning the UBE3A antisense transcript, so its direct transfer value for that mechanism cannot be established from this paper.

papers.title: RNAa-mediated epigenetic attenuation of the cell senescence via locus specific induction of endogenous SIRT1.
papers.summary: The study shows that a locus-specific SIRT1-antagoNAT can knock down the natural antisense transcript SIRT1-NAT and increase SIRT1 expression in human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells. The treatment improved proliferation, reduced senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity, reversed senescence-associated gene-expression changes, and improved differentiation with passage-dependent exceptions; it did not test the UBE3A antisense transcript or Angelman syndrome.

papers.title: Comparative Characterization of a Proposed Generic Nusinersen: Identity of the Oligonucleotide Structure and Equivalence in SMN2 Splicing Activity.
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates that nusinersen and the proposed generic GNR-100 have comparable splice-switching activity in patient-derived SMA fibroblasts, increasing full-length SMN2 mRNA and functional SMN protein. It provides transferable evidence for antisense-oligonucleotide manufacturing, analytical characterization, and cellular activity testing, but it does not mention or act on the UBE3A antisense transcript or Angelman syndrome.

papers.title: Screening de novo designed protein binders in unpurified lysate using flow induced dispersion analysis.
papers.summary: The paper shows that flow-induced dispersion analysis (FIDA) can screen de novo designed protein binders directly in bacterial lysates. FIDA identified ALFA-tag binders and PSD-95 SH3-GK binders, with nanomolar-affinity binders detected for the PSD-95 construct, while heat treatment improved lysate purity and reduced false positives.

papers.title: Development of a Potent Cyclic Peptide Inhibitor of the nNOS/PSD-95 Interaction.
papers.summary: The paper designed and optimized a cyclic nNOS β-hairpin mimetic peptide that potently inhibits the nNOS/PSD-95 interaction, achieving the highest reported affinity for a peptide macrocycle inhibitor of PDZ domains. The study identifies this interaction, including the DLG4-encoded scaffold PSD-95, as a prospective target for acute ischemic stroke therapy, but the abstract does not report in vivo efficacy.

papers.title: Development of Peptide-Based Probes for Molecular Imaging of the Postsynaptic Density in the Brain.
papers.summary: The study developed radiolabeled and fluorescent AVLX-144-derived probes for imaging the DLG4-encoded postsynaptic scaffold PSD-95. Quantitative autoradiography detected reduced probe binding in post-mortem Parkinson’s disease brain slices, suggesting postsynaptic pathology but not establishing a clinical diagnostic.

papers.title: Soluble TREM2 ameliorates pathological phenotypes in ischemic stroke models via modulating neuronal and microglial functions.
papers.summary: The paper reports that soluble TREM2 declines after oxygen-glucose deprivation or transient middle cerebral artery occlusion and protects cultured neurons and ischemic mice by disrupting the nNOS–PSD-95 interaction, promoting microglial activation, and increasing anti-inflammatory cytokine expression. These findings identify sTREM2 as a neuroprotective intervention and PSD-95-associated signaling as the measured synaptic mechanism, although the paper does not name the DLG4 gene.

papers.title: Blocking Src-PSD-95 interaction rescues glutamatergic signaling dysregulation in schizophrenia
papers.summary: The preprint reports that the cell-penetrating Src-activating PSD-95 inhibitory peptide TAT-SAPIP increased postsynaptic Src activity in human and mouse systems and enhanced synaptic NMDA receptor currents in mice. Chronic intracerebroventricular administration also rescued trace fear-conditioning deficits in Src hypomorphic mice, supporting interference with the Src–DLG4 interaction as a therapeutic strategy for schizophrenia and potentially other disorders with NMDA receptor hypofunction.

papers.title: Loberamisal for Acute Ischemic Stroke: The LAIS Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.summary: In a phase 3 randomized clinical trial, intravenous loberamisal, which targets the postsynaptic density 95 pathway and α2-GABAA receptor, increased the proportion of adults with acute ischemic stroke achieving a modified Rankin Scale score of 0–1 at 90 days. The abstract does not name DLG4 or establish that the observed stroke benefit arose specifically through DLG4-encoded PSD-95.

papers.title: Chronic Rapamycin Prevents Electrophysiological and Morphological Alterations Produced by Conditional Pten Deletion in Mouse Cortex.
papers.summary: In mice with conditional Pten deletion from cortical pyramidal neurons, chronic rapamycin prevented enlarged somatic area, altered membrane properties, reduced spontaneous and miniature inhibitory currents, and increased evoked inhibitory-current responses associated with mTORC1 activation. These findings provide experimental evidence that rapamycin can modulate PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling in cortical neurons, but rapamycin also altered physiology in wild-type neurons and its effects on seizure latency were described only as preliminary.

papers.title: MCU knockdown attenuates cisplatin-induced damage of auditory cells: potential involvement of PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling and autophagy-related processes.
papers.summary: In cisplatin-injured HEI-OC1 cells and mouse cochleae, MCU knockdown or Ru360 cotreatment was associated with reduced injury, while genetic knockdown increased PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling and altered autophagy-related markers. These data nominate MCU-related signaling as a modifiable protective mechanism, but pathway causality, autophagic flux, mitochondrial calcium changes, cochlear Ru360 exposure, and target-specific effects remain unconfirmed.

papers.title: Everolimus ameliorates cognitive deficits and synaptic dysfunction in mice with prefrontal cortical ADNP knockdown.
papers.summary: In a mouse model with prefrontal cortical ADNP knockdown, everolimus alleviated behavioral and molecular abnormalities associated with mTORC1 activation, impaired autophagy, synaptic dysfunction, and cognitive deficits. The findings support the mTOR pathway as a therapeutic target for ADNP-related cognitive impairments, but the evidence is preclinical.

papers.title: α-Synuclein Activates Ras–PI3K/AKT/mTOR Signaling to Drive Pathology in Parkinson’s Disease
papers.summary: In α-Syn A53T transgenic mice and α-Syn-containing human and mouse brain systems, α-synuclein increased Ras–PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling, neuronal neutral-lipid accumulation, and pathological α-synuclein species. The brain-penetrant PI3K inhibitor paxalisib reduced α-synuclein pathology and lipid accumulation while restoring AKT phosphorylation, autophagic flux, and lipid homeostasis, supporting PI3K inhibition as a therapeutic strategy for Parkinson’s disease.

papers.title: Terazosin Alleviates Apoptosis and Neuroinflammation in Cerebral Ischemia-reperfusion Injury via Activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR Signaling Pathway.
papers.summary: In a mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion model, terazosin reduced cerebral infarction, neurological deficits, neuronal apoptosis, neuroinflammation, and microglial activation. Mechanistic experiments indicate that these protective effects depend on activation of PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling, because the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 abolished them.

papers.title: Esketamine Ameliorates Propofol-Induced Long-Term Cognitive Impairments in Juvenile Rats by Suppressing Autophagy via Activating the PI3K/Akt/mTOR Signaling Pathway.
papers.summary: In juvenile rats exposed to propofol during neurodevelopment, esketamine ameliorated long-term cognitive impairment, hippocampal neuronal damage, excessive autophagy, and inflammatory cytokine elevation while activating PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling. The study also used the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 and rapamycin as experimental pathway modulators, although their individual results are not reported in the abstract.

papers.title: Synaptic plasticity and NO-cGMP-PKG signaling regulate pre- and postsynaptic alterations at rat lateral amygdala synapses following fear conditioning.
papers.summary: In rats, fear conditioning produced persistent increases in GluR1, synapsin, and synaptophysin expression at lateral-amygdala synapses, and pharmacological blockade of CaMKII, Rho/ROCK, NO-cGMP-PKG, or NMDAR signaling reduced these training-induced changes. The study provides direct evidence for a CaMKII-dependent synaptic-plasticity intervention but does not mention or measure PLCγ-CaMKII/CREB signaling as a complete pathway.

papers.title: Tilianin Ameliorates Cognitive Dysfunction and Neuronal Damage in Rats with Vascular Dementia via p-CaMKII/ERK/CREB and ox-CaMKII-Dependent MAPK/NF-κB Pathways.
papers.summary: In a chronic cerebral-ischemia rat model and an oxygen-glucose-deprivation human-neuron model, tilianin improved cognitive deficits, neuronal degeneration, oxidative injury, apoptosis, and inflammation. Its neuroprotective effects depended on CaMKIIα and involved restoration of hippocampal p-CaMKII/ERK/CREB signaling together with suppression of the ox-CaMKII/MAPK/NF-κB inflammatory pathway.

papers.title: Regular exercise ameliorates high-fat diet-induced depressive-like behaviors by activating hippocampal neuronal autophagy and enhancing synaptic plasticity.
papers.summary: In a high-fat-diet mouse model, regular treadmill exercise reduced depressive-like behavior and hippocampal neuronal damage while restoring Wnt5a/Ca2+/CamkII signaling, neuronal autophagy, synaptic transmission, and synaptic plasticity. The Wnt5a inhibitor Box5 counteracted these exercise-associated benefits, indicating that Wnt5a-dependent signaling was necessary for the observed effects.

papers.title: Gastrodin ameliorates learning and memory impairment in rats with vascular dementia by promoting autophagy flux via inhibition of the Ca2+/CaMKII signal pathway.
papers.summary: In vascular dementia model rats, gastrodin improved learning and memory while reducing hippocampal CaMKIIα phosphorylation and abnormal accumulation of LC3 and p62. In CoCl2-treated HT22 cells, gastrodin restored autophagic flux by lowering intracellular Ca2+ and Ca2+-dependent CaMKII phosphorylation, with CaMKII inhibition or knockdown producing no additional reduction in p62 beyond gastrodin alone. The paper does not mention PLCγ, CREB, or PLCγ-CaMKII/CREB signaling, so transfer of that exact mechanism is not established here.

papers.title: GLYX-13 pretreatment ameliorates long-term isoflurane exposure-induced cognitive impairment in mice.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of prolonged isoflurane exposure, GLYX-13 pretreatment improved contextual fear conditioning and novel object recognition while restoring hippocampal NR2B, CaMKII, and CREB expression and phosphorylation. The CaMKII inhibitor KN93 diminished these molecular and cognitive effects, supporting involvement of the NR2B/CaMKII/CREB pathway rather than directly establishing the transfer mechanism PLCγ-CaMKII/CREB signaling.

papers.title: Simvastatin Enhances Activity and Trafficking of α7 Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor in Hippocampal Neurons Through PKC and CaMKII Signaling Pathways.
papers.summary: Acute simvastatin treatment enhanced α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor activity and membrane trafficking in mouse hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons. The effects depended on reduced farnesyl pyrophosphate/farnesylation and involved PKC phosphorylation for receptor activity and CaMKII-dependent signaling for trafficking, but the paper did not test PLCγ-CaMKII/CREB signaling.

unread.title: Mutation Update for UBE3A variants in Angelman syndrome.
unread.why: A cohort of 2,515 Angelman referrals provides direct evidence for UBE3A variant interpretation and deposits classified variants in ClinVar.

unread.title: Episodic tremors representing cortical myoclonus are characteristic in Angelman syndrome due to UBE3A mutations.
unread.why: The paper characterizes a disabling, previously under-recognized seizure phenotype in UBE3A-mutant Angelman syndrome and reports treatment response to levetiracetam.

unread.title: Angelman syndrome phenotype associated with mutations in MECP2, a gene encoding a methyl CpG binding protein.
unread.why: Screening of clinically diagnosed Angelman cases identified Rett syndrome or Angelman-like phenotypes caused by MECP2 variants, demonstrating the value of an alternate diagnostic test.

unread.title: Decreased tonic inhibition in cerebellar granule cells causes motor dysfunction in a mouse model of Angelman syndrome.
unread.why: The Angelman mouse model demonstrates reduced tonic GABAergic inhibition and shows that THIP corrects Purkinje-cell firing and reduces ataxia in vivo.

unread.title: Investigation of UBE3A and MECP2 in Angelman syndrome (AS) and patients with features of AS.
unread.why: The study directly tested UBE3A and MECP2 in molecularly unresolved Angelman cohorts and defined their diagnostic yield and familial-sporadic distribution.

unread.title: Mice lacking the beta3 subunit of the GABAA receptor have the epilepsy phenotype and many of the behavioral characteristics of Angelman syndrome.
unread.why: Gabrb3 knockout mice reproduce seizures, EEG abnormalities, learning and memory deficits, motor impairments, hyperactivity, and disrupted rest-activity cycles relevant to Angelman syndrome.

unread.title: Angelman syndrome: consensus for diagnostic criteria. Angelman Syndrome Foundation.
unread.why: The paper directly provides consensus diagnostic criteria for Angelman syndrome, a clinically reusable diagnostic and classification standard.

unread.title: An ASO therapy for Angelman syndrome that targets an evolutionarily conserved region at the start of the <i>UBE3A-AS</i> transcript.
unread.why: Reports optimized ASOs that silence UBE3A-AS and restore paternal UBE3A in Angelman patient-derived neurons and nonhuman primates.

unread.title: Levodopa responsive Parkinsonism in adults with Angelman Syndrome.
unread.why: Reports dramatic clinical improvement of Angelman-associated parkinsonism with levodopa in two affected adults.

unread.title: Recommendations by the ClinGen Rett/Angelman-like expert panel for gene-specific variant interpretation methods.
unread.why: Provides and pilot-tests standardized ClinGen criteria for interpreting UBE3A and related neurodevelopmental-disorder variants.

unread.title: A preclinical pig model of Angelman syndrome mirrors the early developmental trajectory of the human condition.
unread.why: Establishes a pig model reproducing major early motor, behavioral, growth, and neurodevelopmental phenotypes of Angelman syndrome.

unread.title: GABAergic Neuron-Specific Loss of Ube3a Causes Angelman Syndrome-Like EEG Abnormalities and Enhances Seizure Susceptibility.
unread.why: Defines a neuron-specific Angelman model and links GABAergic Ube3a loss to EEG abnormalities and increased seizure susceptibility.

unread.title: The spectrum of mutations in UBE3A causing Angelman syndrome.
unread.why: Reports mutation-spectrum data and validates UBE3A sequencing as useful for diagnosing Angelman syndrome after normal methylation analysis.

unread.title: The UBE3A-ATS antisense oligonucleotide rugonersen in children with Angelman syndrome: a phase 1 trial.
unread.why: This first-in-human phase 1 study directly tested an ASO therapy that reinstates paternal UBE3A expression in children with Angelman syndrome and reported safety, target-related EEG changes, and clinical signals.

unread.title: Longitudinal EEG model detects antisense oligonucleotide treatment effect and increased UBE3A in Angelman syndrome.
unread.why: The paper establishes a validated longitudinal EEG model and demonstrates its ability to detect ASO-mediated Ube3A treatment effects in humans and mice.

unread.title: Screening for UBE3A gene mutations in a group of Angelman syndrome patients selected according to non-stringent clinical criteria.
unread.why: The study reports mutation screening in clinically diagnosed Angelman syndrome patients and identifies novel UBE3A mutations, providing diagnostic assay data.

unread.title: UBE3A gene mutations in Finnish Angelman syndrome patients detected by conformation sensitive gel electrophoresis.
unread.why: The study demonstrates sensitive CSGE-based UBE3A mutation screening and shows its utility for confirming diagnosis and genetic counseling in Angelman syndrome.

unread.title: Peripheral markers of the gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)ergic system in Angelman's syndrome.
unread.why: The study directly measures peripheral GABAergic markers in Angelman syndrome and relates them to deletion-associated epilepsy severity, although the biomarker results are contradictory.

unread.title: CaMKIIα hub ligands are unable to reverse known phenotypes in Angelman syndrome mice.
unread.why: The paper directly tested two selective CaMKIIα-modulating compounds in Angelman syndrome mice and found they did not reverse key behavioral, motor, or seizure phenotypes.

unread.title: Region-dependent differences in tonic inhibition underlie epileptic features in Angelman syndrome model mice.
unread.why: The study directly tests mechanistically targeted GABAergic drugs in Angelman syndrome mice and identifies region-specific tonic inhibition and alpha5 GABA_A receptors as a therapeutic avenue.

unread.title: Elevated Delta Power in a Maternal UBE3A -Deletion Pig Model of Angelman Syndrome
unread.why: The maternal UBE3A-deletion pig reproduces the disease-associated EEG phenotype and supports noninvasive, translationally relevant assessment of neural dysfunction and therapeutic responses.

unread.title: Parvalbumin interneurons and dentate gyrus homeostatic dysregulation shape epileptogenesis in Angelman syndrome model mice
unread.why: Cell type-specific deletion and rescue experiments identify PV interneurons and GABAergic UBE3A restoration as experimentally supported approaches for controlling seizure susceptibility.

unread.title: SUBCELLULAR FUNCTIONS OF UBE3A ISOFORMS DRIVE SYNAPTIC DYSFUNCTION IN ANGELMAN SYNDROME
unread.why: Isoform-specific replacement in Angelman model systems experimentally identifies the nuclear and cytosolic UBE3A functions needed for synaptic development.

unread.title: Aberrant accumulation of α-synuclein might be linked with the progressive motor deficits in a mouse model of Angelman syndrome
unread.why: The study provides an Angelman mouse model with progressive motor deficits and data supporting α-synuclein accumulation as a mechanistic biomarker and candidate target.

unread.title: The Angelman Mimic: Navigating Diagnostic Uncertainty in a Genetically Diverse Landscape
unread.why: Testing 39 phenotypically similar patients identified molecular causes in both confirmed Angelman syndrome and genetically distinct Angelman-like cases.

unread.title: Functional neuroimaging identifies a cross-species biomarker for treatment monitoring in Angelman syndrome
unread.why: Visually evoked cortical hemodynamic responses were validated across Angelman mouse models and patients and were normalized by UBE3A restoration, supporting use as a treatment-monitoring endpoint.

unread.title: Targeting UBE3A and downstream estrogen receptor-β signaling to restore oligodendroglial homeostasis in Angelman syndrome
unread.why: A targeted screen identified ESRβ activation, and selective agonists restored oligodendrocyte self-renewal, myelination deficits, and behavioral abnormalities in Angelman model systems.

unread.title: Cell-type-specific dysregulated gene expression in the frontal cortex of an Angelman syndrome pig model
unread.why: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing of Angelman pig cortex provides a cell-type-resolved resource and identifies neuronal pathway and somatostatin abnormalities relevant to disease modeling.

unread.title: A preclinical pig model of Angelman syndrome mirrors the early developmental trajectory of the human condition
unread.why: The maternal UBE3A-deletion pig exhibits developmental, behavioral, communication, growth, and motor abnormalities that mirror early human Angelman syndrome and support preclinical testing.

unread.title: Operant behavior is reliably impaired in a mouse model of Angelman syndrome
unread.why: Operant acquisition and extinction testing reliably quantifies cognitive-like learning impairment in Angelman mice and improves genotype discrimination for preclinical treatment studies.

unread.title: Clinical and Genetic Characterization of Angelman Syndrome in a Chinese Cohort: UBE3A Variant Spectrum Expansion and Utility of Long-read Sequencing
unread.why: A multimodal diagnostic workflow resolved UBE3A variants, deletions, paternal uniparental disomy, parental origin, and suspected low-level germline mosaicism in Angelman syndrome.

unread.title: Neuronal UBE3A loss engages a TNF-driven neuron-to-microglia axis that promotes synapse remodeling
unread.why: Pharmacological TNFR1 inhibition reduced microglial inflammation and synapse engulfment downstream of neuronal UBE3A loss in human cell models and was supported by in vivo datasets.

unread.title: Electrophysiological Phenotype in Angelman Syndrome Differs Between Genotypes.
unread.why: Clinical EEG data from 58 children with Angelman syndrome establish genotype-associated electrophysiological biomarkers that could support stratification and treatment trials.

unread.title: Angelman syndrome: Current and emerging therapies in 2016.
unread.why: The review synthesizes tested and emerging Angelman syndrome interventions, including negative minocycline, levodopa, and dietary trials and preclinical gene-reactivation strategies.

unread.title: Expanding the clinico-molecular spectrum of Angelman syndrome phenotype with the GABRG3 gene: Evidence from methylation and sequencing studies.
unread.why: The study evaluates a diagnostic workflow for unresolved Angelman phenotypes and identifies sequence and methylation abnormalities in GABRG3 using concrete molecular assays.

unread.title: Drowning as a cause of death in Angelman syndrome.
unread.why: This Angelman syndrome case provides direct evidence supporting water supervision as a safety intervention for patients with fascination with water.

unread.title: Gaboxadol in angelman syndrome: A double-blind, parallel-group, randomized placebo-controlled phase 3 study.
unread.why: This Phase 3 trial directly evaluated gaboxadol and the CGI-I-AS outcome in pediatric Angelman syndrome, finding good tolerability but no significant efficacy advantage over placebo.

unread.title: Screening of UBE3A gene in patients referred for Angelman Syndrome.
unread.why: The study demonstrates the diagnostic utility of UBE3A sequencing in unresolved Angelman syndrome cases and identifies alternative genetic causes in phenocopy patients.

unread.title: Anesthetic experience for strabismus surgery in a patient with Angelman syndrome: A case report.
unread.why: The case provides disease-specific anesthetic considerations and a concrete management approach for surgery in a patient with Angelman syndrome.

unread.title: Novel method for detection of UBE3A protein in CSF from individuals with Angelman syndrome.
unread.why: The study validates a sensitive CSF UBE3A assay and shows markedly lower protein concentrations in Angelman syndrome cohorts, making it a reusable pharmacodynamic or translational biomarker.

unread.title: [Epilepsy in Angelman syndrome and the most common electroencephalographic findings].
unread.why: Analysis of 34 video EEGs from 17 patients supports video EEG as a sensitive early diagnostic biomarker and provides reusable EEG outcome patterns for Angelman syndrome.

unread.title: A stem cell-based toolkit to model Angelman syndrome caused by paternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 15.
unread.why: The paper creates and validates a patient-specific iPSC toolkit for the understudied paternal-uniparental-disomy form of Angelman syndrome.

unread.title: Angelman syndrome 2005: updated consensus for diagnostic criteria.
unread.why: This consensus document provides a clinically usable framework for diagnosing Angelman syndrome despite normal or unresolved molecular testing.

unread.title: Induced pluripotent stem cell models of the genomic imprinting disorders Angelman and Prader-Willi syndromes.
unread.why: The paper establishes patient-derived iPSC models that retain the disease-relevant UBE3A imprint and support mechanistic study in human neurons.

unread.title: Distinct phenotypes distinguish the molecular classes of Angelman syndrome.
unread.why: It supplies a standardized clinical dataset and phenotype measures that distinguish molecular classes of Angelman syndrome.

unread.title: Ube3a reinstatement identifies distinct developmental windows in a murine Angelman syndrome model.
unread.why: It directly tests gene-reinstatement therapy in an Angelman syndrome mouse model and defines developmental windows for rescuing specific disease phenotypes.

unread.title: Ube3a-ATS is an atypical RNA polymerase II transcript that represses the paternal expression of Ube3a.
unread.why: The study identifies antisense-transcript repression as a means to activate paternal Ube3a and validates mechanisms in mouse and engineered cell models.

unread.title: Potassium channel dysfunction in human neuronal models of Angelman syndrome.
unread.why: It identifies BK-channel modulation as a testable therapeutic approach and provides human neuronal and mouse evidence that BK antagonists normalize hyperexcitability and reduce seizures.

unread.title: Melatonin for chronic insomnia in Angelman syndrome: a randomized placebo-controlled trial.
unread.why: A randomized placebo-controlled trial in children with Angelman syndrome showed that low-dose melatonin improved several measured sleep outcomes.

unread.title: Double-blind therapeutic trial in Angelman syndrome using betaine and folic acid.
unread.why: A one-year double-blind trial directly tested methylation-promoting betaine and folic acid in 48 children with Angelman syndrome and reported their clinical, biochemical, and EEG outcomes.

unread.title: Decrease in benzodiazepine receptor binding in a patient with Angelman syndrome detected by iodine-123 iomazenil and single-photon emission tomography.
unread.why: The study demonstrates in a patient with Angelman syndrome that iomazenil SPET can quantify reduced GABA-A receptor-associated benzodiazepine binding across brain regions.

unread.title: Behavioral Evaluation of Angelman Syndrome Mice at Older Ages.
unread.why: The study validates aged Ube3A-mutant mice and motor, social, and anxiety-related behavioral assays as preclinical outcome measures for Angelman syndrome.

unread.title: Asystole during outbursts of laughing in a child with Angelman syndrome.
unread.why: The Angelman case provides direct evidence that atropine can prevent laughter-triggered asystole and supports targeted ECG evaluation for related symptoms.

unread.title: Benefit of corticosteroid therapy in Angelman syndrome.
unread.why: Four children with Angelman syndrome showed reduced seizures, normalized EEG characteristics, and improved jerks, sleep, and development after corticosteroid treatment.

unread.title: Bone mineral density in angelman syndrome.
unread.why: The study identifies high osteopenia prevalence in Angelman syndrome and supports routine bone-density screening, especially in patients receiving long-term antiepileptic therapy.

unread.title: Alterations of synaptic plasticity in Angelman syndrome model mice are rescued by 5-HT7R stimulation.
unread.why: LP-211 stimulation directly rescued synaptic-protein synthesis, dendritic spine density, hippocampal long-term potentiation, and fear-conditioning performance in Angelman syndrome mice.

unread.title: Split-cord malformation in a girl with Angelman syndrome: a mere coincidence?
unread.why: The Angelman case supports evaluating the spinal cord when cutaneous stigmata or disproportionate paraparesis suggest split-cord malformation.

unread.title: Imbalanced expression of cation-chloride cotransporters as a potential therapeutic target in an Angelman syndrome mouse model.
unread.why: Bumetanide restored cognitive deficits and reduced seizure susceptibility in an Angelman syndrome mouse model while identifying imbalanced NKCC1/KCC2 expression as a therapeutic target.

unread.title: Strabismus surgery in Angelman syndrome: More than ocular alignment.
unread.why: Strabismus surgery in 17 children with Angelman syndrome achieved alignment in most exotropic cases and was associated with improved walking and fine-motor performance.

unread.title: Multi-targeting zinc finger nuclease vector unsilences paternal UBE3A in a mouse model of Angelman syndrome.
unread.why: AAV-delivered ZFN17/18 reduced Ube3a-ATS and restored paternal UBE3A expression in cultured neurons and an Angelman syndrome mouse brain for at least nine weeks.

unread.title: Vagal nerve stimulation for medically refractory epilepsy in Angelman syndrome: a series of three cases.
unread.why: Vagal nerve stimulation reduced seizures beyond the prior medication benefit in all three children with medically refractory Angelman syndrome epilepsy.

unread.title: Recovery of Angelman syndrome rat deficits with UBE3A protein supplementation.
unread.why: Exogenous UBE3A restored hippocampal long-term potentiation in Angelman syndrome rat slices and rescued associative learning and memory deficits after intrahippocampal administration in vivo.

unread.title: Dietary Intake of Octanoic Acid Restores UBE3A Expression and Improves the Behavioral Phenotypes in a Mouse Model of Angelman Syndrome.
unread.why: Dietary octanoic acid reactivated paternal Ube3a in neurons and improved selected behavioral and dendritic-spine abnormalities in Angelman syndrome mouse models.

unread.title: Association between sleep disturbances and challenging behavior in children and adolescents with Angelman syndrome.
unread.why: Registry data from 109 participants identified behavioral predictors and a regression model for sleep disturbances in children and adolescents with Angelman syndrome.

unread.title: [Anesthetic management of a child with Angelman's syndrome].
unread.why: A documented anesthetic approach enabled successful surgery in a child with Angelman syndrome and provides concrete precautions for airway management, temperature, heart rate, and respiratory depression.

unread.title: Identification of the genetic basis of pediatric neurogenetic disorders at a tertiary referral hospital in Indonesia: Contribution of whole exome sequencing.
unread.why: Whole-exome sequencing successfully identified a pathogenic UBE3A variant in a pediatric neurodevelopmental cohort, supporting its use as a diagnostic tool for Angelman syndrome.

unread.title: Successful use of cannabidiol in nonconvulsive status epilepticus in Angelman syndrome.
unread.why: Reports successful clinical use of cannabidiol to treat nonconvulsive status epilepticus in a patient with Angelman syndrome.

unread.title: Factors associated with sleep disturbances in children and adolescents with Angelman Syndrome.
unread.why: Provides a validated clinical sleep outcome measure and registry-based analysis of predictors of sleep disturbances in Angelman syndrome.

unread.title: Atypical alpha oscillatory EEG dynamics in children with Angelman syndrome.
unread.why: Identifies and validates quantitative EEG markers of atypical neural maturation in children with Angelman syndrome that could support clinical-trial endpoints.

unread.title: The elusive Angelman syndrome critical region.
unread.why: Provides DNA mapping and a novel polymorphic marker for delimiting the Angelman syndrome critical region and analyzing relevant families.

unread.title: Generation of an induced pluripotent stem cell line from a patient with Angelman syndrome carrying UBE3A mutation.
unread.why: Reports an established patient-derived iPSC model carrying a UBE3A mutation for studying Angelman syndrome biology and treatments.

unread.title: Angelman syndrome with mosaic paternal uniparental disomy suggestive of mitotic nondisjunction.
unread.why: Reports diagnostic testing that identifies mosaic paternal uniparental disomy and supports characterization of an Angelman syndrome molecular subtype.

unread.title: Remote EEG acquisition in Angelman syndrome using PANDABox-EEG.
unread.why: Develops and validates a feasible remote EEG protocol that reliably captures Angelman syndrome-associated delta activity for clinical and research use.

unread.title: A human Angelman Syndrome class II pluripotent stem cell line with fluorescent paternal <i>UBE3A</i> reporter.
unread.why: Provides a human Angelman syndrome cellular model with a fluorescent UBE3A reporter for monitoring gene reactivation and screening therapeutic candidates.

unread.title: A prodrug targeting CIM6P/IGF2R enhances memory in healthy mice and reverses deficits in an Angelman syndrome mouse model.
unread.why: Shows that the small-molecule prodrug PMP1 improves memory and motor deficits in an Angelman syndrome mouse model through CIM6P/IGF2R.

unread.title: Generation of isogenic models of Angelman syndrome and Prader-Willi syndrome in CRISPR/Cas9-engineered human embryonic stem cells
unread.why: The authors report isogenic human embryonic stem-cell models of major Angelman genetic subtypes that enable allele-specific studies and therapeutic testing.

unread.title: Three-Dimensional Gait Analysis of School-Age Children With Angelman Syndrome: A Case-Control Study.
unread.why: The case-control study validates quantitative 3D gait metrics for measuring the characteristic unstable, prancing gait of Angelman syndrome.

unread.title: Lower respiratory rate during sleep in children with angelman syndrome compared to age-matched controls.
unread.why: The study validates a non-invasive digital biomarker and monitoring method for measuring sleep-associated respiratory abnormalities in Angelman syndrome.

unread.title: Cell Type-Specific Contributions of UBE3A to Angelman Syndrome Behavioral Phenotypes.
unread.why: Mouse experiments demonstrate that reinstatement of Ube3a in specific neuronal populations rescues distinct behavioral and sleep phenotypes, directly informing cell-targeted gene therapy.

unread.title: A Drosophila model for Angelman syndrome.
unread.why: The study establishes multiple genetically defined Drosophila models that reproduce key Angelman phenotypes and can be reused for UBE3A substrate and therapeutic screens.
